headline: Highest risk is broad-network research agent ingesting content-writing outputs, creating medium prompt-injection and data-leakage exposure; other pairwise risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runnable isolation, while agent B can read files, browse, and use MCP. If A’s prompts or generated content are fed into B, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared path is inferred from docs only, so I choose medium over low because the interaction is plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF agent A outputs prompt text that agent B ingests as instructions
IF agent B loads A-derived files through filesystem, browser, or MCP without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a provenance tag to all A-derived files
Require a human review step before B executes instructions from content
Restrict B to a read-only staging folder
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/quote separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches local documents, citations, images, and multiple API backends, while agent A is a docs-only prompt source with no network egress. If A’s outputs are stored in the same workspace as B’s research inputs, B can upload or summarize sensitive local files to third parties. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A-derived prompts or notes are placed in the same workspace as B’s research files
IF B is configured to send local documents or citations to external APIs
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from B’s input directory
Turn off external API connectors in B for the run
Use a throwaway API key with minimal scope
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or runnable surfaces; B has filesystem read, browser, subprocess, and package install, but no shared mutable target with A is documented. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely. I keep this low rather than none because the profiles are incomplete and B’s multi-instance research model could still collide with external shared resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF B is extended with write access to a shared directory or git repo
mitigations: Keep A read-only and non-runnable
Run B in a separate working directory
Avoid shared git or database targets
Serialize any manual handoff between agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt/content source and B is a research agent with planner/execution/publisher roles, so A’s text can become B’s input and then B’s output without a documented verification barrier. That creates a realistic cascade where untrusted prompt content is rendered as research guidance or citations. The interaction is inferred from docs, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as source material or instructions
IF B publishes outputs without a separate verification step
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources, not A outputs
Insert a verification checklist before publishing
Mark A content as untrusted in B’s prompt
Limit B to summarization only for A-derived inputs
requires-engineering: add automated source-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles local documents, citations, images, and third-party APIs, while A is a docs-only open-source prompt repository. If regulated or personal data is routed through B, its external API calls and retention behavior can create compliance mismatch. A is not the compliance driver here, so only B is cited for the concrete residency/retention risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in B’s research inputs
IF B sends those inputs to external APIs without a DPA or residency controls
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B runs
Use region-locked API endpoints
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly
Document retention and deletion settings
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
